Subject: RE: Competitive eval - model quality follow-up — initial smoke results

Samir / Priya — attaching the promised smoke-run artifacts and a short summary. We ran the 50-prompt starter set across the requested variants. Files attached: eval-results-acme-v1.csv (raw per-prompt outputs + flags) and redwood-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (1-page summary). High-level findings below: 

Summary (50 prompts):
- Hallucination rate: redwood-1.0 = 3.8% (2/50), redwood-quant = 4.6% (3/50), openai-gpt4 = 5.1% (3/50), vertex/anthropic = 6.9% (4/50).
- Exact match / correctness: redwood-1.0 88%, openai-gpt4 85%, vertex/anthropic 82%
- Instruction-following (multi-step): redwood models passed 46/50, vendors 43/50
- Latency (p95): redwood-1.0 220ms, redwood-quant 180ms, vendor calls averaged 260-420ms depending on provider and network overhead

Caveats & methodology: small sample (50 prompts) — results are directional. Prompts were normalized for system messages and tokenization differences. For hallucination labeling we used a binary human-in-the-loop check (Neha validated edge cases).

Next steps we propose:
1) Run the full 500-prompt suite (we estimate 7 business days).
2) Add targeted PII redaction tests and end-to-end verification for a small subset of production queries.
3) Review the results together — can we schedule a 30-minute readout next week? I'm available Tue/Wed morning PT.

If you want a deeper breakdown (per-prompt examples of hallucinations), we can include a table in the next PDF.

Thanks — Marissa
Attachments: eval-results-acme-v1.csv, redwood-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf
